principle: A car can hold distance in many places and they do not mean the same thing. Each place is read separately, kept with the exact request, the exact reply bytes and the public definition it came from, and compared only with places of the same kind. A difference is reported as an observation with the reasons that could explain it. Nothing here concludes that a car was tampered with, and nothing names an original mileage.

comparisonRules: Only values of the same measurement are compared. 'Current odometer copies' are compared with each other and with nothing else.
The reference is the highest usable current reading. Records of the past are compared with that reference, never with each other.

A record of the past that is higher than the highest current reading is reported as an observation with the amount, the module, the event and the raw reply. It is not called tampering: a replaced module, a repaired or replaced cluster, a wrong definition, a unit confusion or a corrupted counter produce the same picture.
An installation record is read under both of its possible meanings (the odometer at installation, or the distance since). Only what holds under both is concluded from it.
Component counters (catalytic converter, traction battery) restart when the component is replaced and are kept apart; they are neither compared nor added up.
A zero or an all-ones value in a record is 'no record', not a distance.
When fewer than two current copies exist, the page says that nothing can be compared. It does not fall back to a single value being 'confirmed'.
A read that fails (no reply, negative reply, a reply from another module, an implausible value) is kept in the list of attempts with its reason. It never erases a reading that succeeded.

sources.title: Standard odometer, SAE J1979 Mode 01 PID A6
sources.request: 01 A6 (optional; advertised in the ECU's supported-PID bitmaps)
sources.reply: 4 data bytes A B C D: (A*2^24 + B*2^16 + C*2^8 + D) / 10 km
sources.scope: Any vehicle whose engine ECU implements the optional PID. Which vehicles do is not known.
sources.observed: PID A6 returned NO DATA in all four recorded capture files (Volt 2013, BMW 320i 2018, Ford Escape 2012, Toyota Camry); consistent with an optional PID, and no finding about those cars' other modules.
caveats: The responding ECU is not identified.
The standard itself (paid) was not read; the formula was confirmed on the public PID list.

sources.title: Standard distance and time context, PIDs 21, 31, 4D, 4E
sources.appStatus: implemented before this work (GenericObdDistanceContextProvider). Context only; never the odometer and never compared with it.
caveats: Resets when codes are cleared; says nothing about total distance.

sources.title: Module copies of the total odometer (OBDb, services 22 and 21)
sources.request: 22 <identifier> (or 21 <local identifier> for KWP2000) to the module the definition names
sources.reply: Decoded with the definition's bit offset, length, scale and unit
sources.scope: Exact model only (never the identifiers of another model). Counts and module types are in the generated tables.
sources.appStatus: implemented before this work (CatalogOdometerProvider, first pass, at most 16 requests); the name classifier that keeps this group clean is new
caveats: About half of the definitions are flagged debug by the community.
A row cannot be restricted to a model year.

Some definitions are unusable on purpose: a unit that is not a distance (Ford 'Transmission odometer' is declared in celsius, some Toyota 'Total distance' rows are 'scalar'), a field wider than 32 bits, or a module address that cannot be resolved safely. The page does not request them.

sources.title: Odometer stored when something happened (adaptation, warning, DPF regeneration, replacement, TPMS event, service)
sources.reply: As above; zero and all-ones mean 'no record'
sources.scope: Exact model only; second pass, at most 10 requests, after the current values.
caveats: A record of the past: shown separately and compared only with the highest current reading.

sources.title: Value tied to a module's installation ('Mileage / Odometer with ECU installed')
caveats: The definition does not say whether the value is the odometer at installation or the distance since; only what holds under both meanings is concluded.

sources.title: Component distance counters (catalytic converter, traction battery)
sources.appStatus: classified and kept apart in this work; never compared
caveats: Restarts when the component is replaced.

sources.title: Distance-like values that are not snapshots (since, remaining, before, after, average, until, request, raw count)
sources.appStatus: never requested by the Mileage page (classified Excluded in this work)
caveats: Several of these were previously mistaken for the odometer.

sources.title: Passive CAN odometer broadcast (listen only)
sources.request: none: the adapter only listens to one frame id for a short time
sources.reply: The frame field of the profile (see canBroadcast in this file)
sources.scope: GM Volt (OVMS), Toyota / Lexus, Honda, Hyundai / Kia, Ford and VW families, per the profiles of BroadcastOdometerProvider; a gateway often hides the frame from the OBD connector.
sources.appStatus: implemented before this work; a value is kept only when two frames agree
caveats: The profiles are family-wide; only Prius 2017 and Lexus CT200h 2018 are in the verified-profile registry, and that registry says 'exact platform profile only'.

sources.title: Odometer fields of opendbc that the app does not listen to
sources.scope: Rivian, additional Hyundai, VW and Ford frames
sources.appStatus: not implemented. Each needs a decoder that does not require a unit field and the evidence of the exact vehicle.
caveats: Several definitions give no unit or scale.

sources.title: Odometer inside a trouble code's snapshot or extended data (UDS service 19)
sources.reply: A list of data identifiers chosen by the manufacturer
sources.appStatus: not implemented. No source says that snapshots carry the odometer; the content is manufacturer-defined. The project's own captures got NO DATA for 19 04 on the BMW.
caveats: Without a manufacturer description of the record, a number in a snapshot cannot be called a mileage.

sources.title: Odometer values of further control units read by workshop tools
sources.scope: A Bosch tester is reported to list the mileage stored in various control units, with the seat memory and the electronic parking assistant named as examples, and to compare them with the speedometer.
sources.appStatus: not implemented. The existence of such readings is documented; the requests are not.
caveats: A trade-press report and a blog; no protocol detail. A disagreement can come from a counter that overflowed: one published case has a transmission module reporting about three times the dashboard value and being judged a corrupted counter.

sources.title: A place found earlier on this phone
sources.scope: This phone and this car only
sources.appStatus: implemented before this work (OdometerFinderService); found by matching a number the user typed, so it is not independently documented
caveats: Evidence of a match, not of a definition.
